JUSTIFICATION REVIEW DOCUMENT

FAR Part 6 Justification and Approval for Other than Full and Open Competition PROGRAM/EQUIPMENT: Design Build of the New World Screwworm (NWS) Sterile Fly Production Facility AUTHORITY: 10 United States Code 3204(a)(2) as implemented in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency

ESTIMATEDAMOUNT:

PREPARED BY CONTRACTING OFFICER TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS SIGNATURES ARE REQUIRED BELO..

I have reviewed this justification and find it adequate to support Other Than Full and Open Competition.

PROGRAM MANAGER SMALL BUSINESS SCO OFFICE OF COUNSEL SENIOR CONTRACTING OFFICIAL HQ OFFICE OF COUNSEL COMMAND ADVOCATE FOR COMPETITION HEAD OF THE CONTRACTING ACTIVITY (HCA) 1 Control Number: SWF-26-0001 FAR Part 6 Justification and Approval for Other than Full and Open Competition

1. Requiring Activity: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Animal and Plant Inspection Service.

2. Contracting Activity: United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District (SWF), 819 Taylor Street, Fort Worth, Texas, 76102.

3. Description of Action: This Justification and Approval authorizes the use of Other than Full and Open Competition---Unusual and Compelling Urgency-- to limit issuance of the Phase I design build competition to 5 contractors, as follows:

The firm-fixed-price Design-Build standalone contract is for the immediate design and construction of a new domestic New World Screwworm (NWS) Sterile Fly Production Facility at Moore Airfield, Hidalgo County, Texas. This facility, funded by USDA Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) appropriations, is urgently needed to support the USDA's efforts to prevent a devastating NWS outbreak in the United States. While the standard solicitation period is 30 days, the Government has determined that issuing the Phase I solicitation will be accelerated but allow for competitive proposals and will balance the limited responses in the sources sought with the unusual and compelling urgency of the mission. USACE expects more than one offeror even with the shortened Phase I solicitation period.

4. Description of Supplies/Services: The USDA requires, with extreme urgency, a design-build standalone "C" type contract for a specialized, complex facility dedicated to the mass rearing and sterilization of NWS flies. This facility will produce up to 300 million sterile flies per week. This production capability is essential for the USDA's Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) program aimed at preventing the spread of NWS into the U.S. and protecting the nation's livestock and wildlife. The facility must be designed and constructed to meet stringent biosecurity and containment requirements to ensure effective production of sterile flies for the eradication program. Execution of the project may require appropriate brand name equipment for the irradiation technique and diet mixer and/or installation of such items by directed subcontractors who can deliver equipment in an expedited manner and perform any required commissioning necessary to meet mission requirements.

Secretary Rollins has determined that the overall goal is to have a complete facility that can produce 300 million sterile flies per week. Given the urgency of the threat, USDA is open to a phased approach to achieve this goal. The anticipated period of performance Control Number: SWF-26-0001 to construct a facility to produce 100 million sterile flies per week is 12-18 months. The work on the remaining 200 million flies per week capacity would be conducted in parallel, as either an expansion of the original facility or as a second facility. Design and construction of the remaining production capabilities beyond the first 100 million may take up to 48 months. The estimated value of this procurement is ███████████

5. Authority Cited: 10 United States Code 3204(a)(2) as implemented in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

6. Reason for Authority Cited: a. Background: The NWS is a parasitic fly larva that infests warm-blooded animals, causing severe pain, tissue damage, and potentially fatal secondary infections. Historically, NWS infestations have devastated livestock industries across the Americas, resulting in significant economic losses and disrupting local economies. The United States successfully eradicated NWS in the 1960s through the innovative SIT, which involves releasing sterile male flies to disrupt the reproductive cycle. Following the lead, Mexico also eradicated the fly, and this led to the Panama–United States Commission for the Eradication and Prevention of Screwworm (COPEG), an organization created to stop the screw worm from going north of Panama. After the eradication, economic and health effects became a direct benefit to society.

After decades of successful eradication, recent NWS outbreaks in Mexico and Central America now present a serious threat as of late September 2025. Just 70 miles from the U.S. border a cow had a confirmed case. These outbreaks have prompted the USDA to suspend live animal imports from Mexico and launch containment plans, including sterile fly production and dispersal facilities. To combat this threat, Secretary of Agriculture launched a comprehensive five-pronged plan, one aspect of which is what this proposal enables. The competition limitation supported by this J&A directly supports the fourth prong of the USDA’s plan: "Take the Fight to the Screwworm," and protects US economy and public health. Limiting the Phase I solicitation to the 5 highly qualified contractors and providing a response time of up to twenty-one days, ensures the prompt delivery of actionable proposals that will greatly increase success, while also providing sufficient time to meaningfully prepare quality phase 1 proposals. Additionally, the proposals will likely need to incorporate long lead brand name equipment for the irradiation technique and diet mixer and/or to be installed by directed subcontractors that manufactured the equipment and specialized biolab security commissioning agents. These measures enable the Government to meet the urgent need for this facility by minimizing evaluation time, focusing resources on the most capable firms, and expediting contract award. b. Alternatives: Several alternatives to this justification were considered:

1) Conducting a Competitive Acquisition: The most obvious alternative is full and open competition. However, the time required for preparing the solicitation, issuing a solicitation, evaluating proposals, and documenting the down select from an unlimited 3 Control Number: SWF-26-0001 pool of potential offerors would result in unacceptable delays. Any delays to this acquisition would increase the risk of a widespread NWS outbreak, causing significant economic and public health damage (as discussed below). Specifically, a full and open competition with unlimited potential offerors would require a minimum of 45 days for proposal submission (15 days for presolicitation and 30 days for Phase 1 solicitation) and 90 days for evaluation and down-select documentation, resulting in a total delay of approximately 135 days. Any delays to this acquisition would increase the risk of a widespread NWS outbreak, causing significant economic and public health damage (as discussed below). Conversely, limiting the Phase 1 offerors to 5 qualified contractors ensures that the evaluation time is limited and spent on quality proposals. Limiting competition to these qualified contractors, considered technically equipped to provide beneficial results to the government, is anticipated to reduce the 135-day time span to only 90 days. This is why only a limited number is required.

2) Extension of an Existing Contract: There are no existing contracts suitable for the rapid design and construction of a facility with the specific biosecurity and production requirements of the NWS sterile fly production facility. There are no contracts currently in place that could meet the size and scope of this requirement.

3) Use of In-House Resources: The USACE does not have sufficient in-house resources to design and construct a facility of this magnitude within the required timeframe. This would require hiring new personnel and developing the necessary expertise, resulting in unacceptable delays. c. Impact if not approved: Disapproval of this J&A would have catastrophic consequences for the U.S. economy and public health, leaving the nation vulnerable to a devastating outbreak of NWS in the US. The implications extend far beyond the state of Texas and represent a significant threat to the entire country. As mentioned in the Background section, Texas already experienced significant risk due to its proximity to Mexico. Other risks include the following:

1) Economic Devastation, Nationwide1: A widespread NWS infestation would cripple the U.S. agricultural sector. While the potential $1.8 billion loss to the Texas economy is alarming, it only represents a fraction of the potential nationwide impact. Texas is a major producer of beef, cotton, and other agricultural commodities. A disruption to Texas agriculture would ripple through national supply chains, impacting food prices, availability, and the profitability of countless businesses. Texas is the largest cattle producing state. If the screwworm decimated Texas herds, the price of beef would skyrocket nationwide. Restaurants would face higher costs, consumers would pay more at the grocery store, and the entire beef supply chain would be thrown into chaos. Other agricultural sectors are similar. An NWS outbreak would lead to increased prices for everything from dairy products and wool to cotton, impacting 1 USDA. (n.d.). NWS Economic Impact Report. USDA Animal and Plant Inspection Service. https://www.aphis.usda.gov/sites/default/files/nws-historical-economic-impact.pdf 4 Control Number: SWF-26-0001 clothing manufacturers, textile mills, and the retail sector.2 Beyond direct agricultural impacts, an NWS outbreak would negatively impact related industries, such as transportation, processing, and retail. Rural communities that rely on agriculture would be particularly hard hit, potentially leading to job losses and economic hardship. Additionally, consider the tourism industry. Hunting, fishing, and other outdoor activities are vital to many state economies. Wildlife infestations would devastate ecotourism, impacting guide services, hotels, restaurants, and other businesses.

Rate 9.10% - Sheep & Goat Cost/Case $32.38 $137.56 $179.61 Total Cattle Cost $121,307,258 $515,351,210 $672,897,355 Total Sheep & Goat Cost $10,769,588 $45,752,456 $59,738,286 Texas Producers Losses $132,076,846 $561,103,666 $732,635,641 Texas Economy Loss $329,598,005 $1,400,235,237 $1,828,293,838 2) National Public Health Crisis: While less common in humans, NWS infestations can be a serious threat, particularly to vulnerable populations (children, the elderly, individuals with compromised immune systems). The maggots burrow into open wounds, causing intense pain, tissue damage, and potentially life-threatening secondary infections. An outbreak would overwhelm the public health system, requiring increased medical surveillance, diagnostic testing, and specialized treatment facilities. It would also necessitate widespread public awareness campaigns to educate people about the risks and how to prevent infestations. The resulting surge in medical costs, coupled with lost productivity due to illness, would further strain the U.S. economy.

3) Erosion of International Trade and Reputation: An NWS outbreak would damage the reputation of the U.S. as a reliable exporter of agricultural products, leading to trade restrictions and economic losses. Trading partners would be hesitant to import U.S. goods, fearing contamination. This would negatively impact the U.S. trade balance and undermine its position as a global leader in agriculture.

4) Threat to National Security: A widespread disruption to the U.S. agricultural sector would threaten the nation's food security and economic stability, posing a national security risk. Access to safe and affordable food is essential for maintaining a stable society. An NWS outbreak could lead to food shortages, price increases, and social unrest.

2 New World Screwworm outbreak in Central America and Mexico. Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service. (n.d.). Accessed September 26, 2025, https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultrydisease/cattle/ticks/screwworm/outbreak-central-america 5 Control Number: SWF-26-0001 5) Animal Welfare: Animals would experience suffering for extended periods of time. Farmers would be forced to take action including euthanizing the animals, to help alleviate the issue. d. The design-build approach with the appropriate brand name equipment to be installed by directed subcontractors, combined with restricting competition, is the only viable strategy to address this unusual and compelling urgency and avert these potentially catastrophic consequences. Failure to approve this J&A would directly impede the USDA's ability to implement its NWS eradication plan. The immediate construction of the sterile fly production facility is essential for producing the volume of sterile flies needed to effectively suppress the NWS population along the U.S.-Mexico border. Without this facility, any delay in award will continue to expose the cattle industry to the risk of NWS infestation, resulting in economic devastation for producers and significant financial obligations for the Government related to outbreak response, containment, and potential trade disruptions. Therefore, an unusual and compelling urgency exists, requiring the expedited completion of this acquisition to mitigate these risks and enable the USDA to begin eradicating the NWS threat to the U.S. economy.

7. Efforts to Obtain Competition: To balance the urgent need for a NWS Sterile Fly Production Facility with the requirement to obtain competition to the maximum extent practicable, USACE Fort Worth will issue a request for proposal to the 5 contractors. As discussed in the market research section below, USACE and USDA used concerted efforts to ensure requirements were not unduly restrictive while still meeting the key aspects of the requirement. The market research determined that 5 contractors were technically capable and expressed interest in the project during the market research process. The notice required at FAR 5.201 will not be published based on the exception at FAR 5.202(a)(2), Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

8. Actions to Increase Competition: SWF is mindful of the requirement in FAR 6.302-2 to request offers from as many potential sources as is practicable under the circumstances, and therefore conducted a robust search and evaluation of potential sources following the procedures outlined in Paragraph 9, Market Research. However, to expedite the design build procurement with the appropriate brand name equipment to be installed by directed subcontractors to address the USDA identified National Emergency there is a need to limit an offer from more than 5 sources under Phase I or enter into negotiations with more than three in Phase II.

9. Market Research: In accordance with FAR Part 10 and DFARS 210.001, thorough market research was conducted to identify all qualified sources capable of fulfilling the urgent requirement for the design and construction of a domestic NWS Sterile Fly Production Facility. USACE worked with the USDA Contracting office, they were able to help identify potential firms based on historical knowledge of contractors they've worked with. However, USDA has limited recent knowledge of construction firms. a. Small Business Database: A search of the Dynamic Small Business Search Database shows no small business firms capable of executing the requirement in Texas 6 Control Number: SWF-26-0001 at sufficient bonding capacity. There are 29 small businesses registered in Texas under the appropriate NAICS but none had a bonding capacity over $100M. b. Sources Sought: To maximize awareness of this opportunity, USACE and USDA directly reached out to over 400 vendors to notify potential offerors of the sources sought announcement. This action also included the USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS)contact list that has vendors who are likely able to handle projects of these sorts. The Sources Sought was posted to SAM.gov on 2 October with a response date of 14 October 2025. c. There were 11 responses to Sources Sought Notice W9126G26R1AS7, as shown in the table below. Of the 11 responses, two firms were not construction contractors, one firm was a small business who did not possess the required bonding capacity or specialized experience, and one firm did not demonstrate enough recent and relevant experience for further consideration. While market research shows many firms performing design or construction projects, the offerors were experienced in either design or construction, not both, and not at biosafety level (BSL) 2 or BSL 3.

1) USDA APHIS BSL guidelines establish procedures for handling infectious agents that pose risks to animals, plants, and the environment. APHIS utilizes these biosafety levels, which range from BSL-1 to BSL-4, and a specialized version called BSL-3-Ag (for agricultural research), to regulate laboratory work and ensure public and environmental safety. The level of biosafety required depends on the risk of the agent. This can include specific requirements for personal protective equipment (PPE), laboratory design, decontamination procedures, and waste management. The production of sterile flies for research or pest control, often requiring BSL2 or BSL3 containment, demands particular attention to these guidelines, especially regarding facility design and construction.

2) Due to the intricate design and specialized construction requirements of a BSL2/BSL3 sterile fly production facility, including stringent containment and environmental controls, experience with both design and construction under a single entity is critical. This integrated approach minimizes communication gaps, reduces coordination challenges, and ensures seamless execution, ultimately mitigating risks to project success. Most vendors were also more experienced with subcontracting; or were responsible for construction management services only.

The market research, including extensive outreach and analysis of submitted responses, identified 5 firms ( that appear to possess the capabilities and experience most likely to successfully execute this technically complex and time-sensitive project. These firms demonstrate the necessary bonding capacity, relevant experience in design-build projects, and a track record of successful construction within regulated environments.

10. Interested Sources: To date, no other sources have written to express interest.

11. Other Facts: a. Procurement history. This action is a novel requirement for the United States and more specifically USACE. While the SIT has been used to combat the NWS, and while the USDA has been contributing to the effort for a number of years, there has never been a domestic production facility constructed and operated within the United States for this purpose. The primary NWS production facility is located in Pacora, Panama. This facility is operated by the Panama-United States Commission for the Eradication and Prevention of Screwworm (COPEG) and funded by the USDA and Panama's Ministry of Agriculture.

However, as COPEG is a bi-national commission, the facility in Panama was not established or operated under U.S. Federal contracting law and regulations. Therefore, there is no directly applicable procurement history within the U.S. Federal system for a facility of this type. b. Other facts. None 9 Control Number: SWF-26-0001

14. Fair and Reasonable Cost Determination: I hereby determine that the anticipated price to the Government for this contract action will be fair and reasonable. The Contracting Officer will determine the price fair and reasonable through limited competition and a negotiation process focused on maximizing value within the established budget. The Government will leverage the budget as a basis to negotiate enhancements and betterments, ensuring they align with project requirements and offer a demonstrable return. A detailed price analysis, using independent government estimates, will validate the value of proposed enhancements. This competitive negotiation approach ensures the final contract price reflects the optimal balance of price and performance within the budget constraints, thus establishing a fair and reasonable price.

[redacted] Contracting Officer

15. Contracting Officer Certification: I certify that this justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief.

[redacted] Contracting Officer 10 Control Number: SWF-26-0001 Approval Based on the foregoing justification, I hereby approve the procurement of Design Build of the New World Screwworm (NWS) Sterile Fly Production Facility on an other than full and open competition basis pursuant to the authority of Title 10 U.S.C. §3204(a)(2) as implemented in FAR 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Urgency. The anticipated performance period to meet USDA production goal is to construct a facility to produce 100 million sterile flies per week is 12-18 months. The remaining production goal of 200 million flies per week capacity may up to 48 months. The approval is subject to availability of funds, and provided that the supplies and/or services herein described have otherwise been authorized for this acquisition.
